references.text: Earlier verses describing the rings on the breastplate and the shoulder pieces of the ephod, which form the basis for the fastening mechanism described in verse 28.
Parallel account of carrying out the instructions, where the breastplate was attached to the ephod with a blue cord through the rings so that it would not come loose.
Description of the construction of the ephod and the band (חֵשֶׁב) over which the breastplate was to rest.
Refers to the robe beneath the ephod, showing the layered structure of the high priest's garments where the breastplate was an integral part.
Describes the dressing of Aaron with the breastplate and the ephod during the consecration, illustrating the practical use of the fastening mechanism.
Describes the preparation (attaching rings to the breastplate) that immediately leads to the binding described in the source verse.
Describes the placement of the rings on the breastplate, which is the prerequisite for the binding described in the source verse.
